articles.title: Tinto Brass, director of Caligula and maestro of Euro erotica, dies aged 93
articles.summary: The cult Italian film-maker began as an assistant to Roberto Rossellini but moved into sex films, believing ‘eroticism to be a fundamental key to human expression’ Italian film director Tinto Brass, who was once hailed as the “Antonioni of the 70s” but came to be better known for bringing Italian…
body: His wife Caterina Varzi and children Bonifacio and Beatrice Brass announced the news of the director’s death to Italian press agency Ansa on Wednesday.

Born in Milan and raised in Venice, Brass first started working in cinema after moving to Paris, where he was an editor and archivist at the Cinémathèque. Upon returning to Italy, he worked as an editor and assistant director to Roberto Rossellini.

His experimental and anarchic approach to film quickly earned him a reputation, and in 1964 he was commissioned by Umberto Eco to create two short films experimenting with visual language for the Triennale di Milano. Warner Bros reportedly approached him to direct A Clockwork Orange, though scheduling conflicts meant the film was offered to Stanley Kubrick instead.

In the 1970s, Brass moved on to erotic cinema. Though crass and filled with nudity, his first steps in the genre were also politically minded explorations of the relationships between sex, power and money.

articles.title: Skydance Reorgs TV and Streaming Distribution Leadership Team Post-Merger, Eight Execs to Exit
articles.summary: Skydance has reshuffled its TV and streaming distribution team, which is responsible for content deals with pay-TV operators, streaming and device platforms, and other partners. As part of the changes, eight execs who were with Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery are departing.
body: Hopkins’ two top lieutenants heading the distribution team are Sarah Bergman, an HBO veteran who most recently was WBD’s EVP of networks and streaming distribution, and Mickey Carter, formerly EVP of distribution for Paramount. Bergman and Carter will share the title of EVP of distribution and they will split responsibility for negotiating distribution agreements and managing partnerships.
The Skydance distribution team handles deals for CBS owned-and-operated stations, 55 basic cable networks, Paramount+, HBO Max, Discovery+, Pluto TV and over 100 FAST channels.

The execs leaving Skydance are: Rivka Golomb (WBD head of distribution strategy and finance), Kelly Kane (WBD SVP partner marketing), Jeff Cross (WBD EVP, legal, distribution and commercial partnerships), Rich Palermo (WBD EVP network and streaming distribution), David Comisar (CBS, SVP, affiliate distribution), Kurt Davis (EVP, CBS affiliate relations), Deena Demasi (Paramount, EVP of marketing, distribution and business development) and Ken Kay (Showtime, EVP of distribution and affiliate marketing).

articles.title: Cynthia Erivo to Play Tupac Shakur’s Mother in Snoop Dogg Biopic
articles.summary: Tony, Grammy, and Emmy winner Cynthia Erivo has joined the cast of Universal’s upcoming Snoop Dogg biopic and is set to portray Tupac’s mother, Afeni Shakur. Jonathan Daviss stars in “Snoop,” which is described as the “definitive biopic of the entertainment mogul and icon,” Snoop Dogg.
body: Afeni Shakur — the late mother of rapper Tupac was a prominent member of the Black Panther Party.

Born in North Carolina as Alice Faye Williams in 1947, Afeni Shakur moved to the Bronx with her mother as an 11-year-old. She joined the Panthers after hearing Bobby Seale speak in 1968, and married fellow Black Panther member Lumumba Shakur soon after.

Craig Brewer (“Hustle and Flow,” “Song Sung Blue”) is directing “Snoop,” which Universal dated for theatrical release on Aug. 6, 2027, based on his rewrite of Joe Robert Cole’s (“Black Panther, “”Wakanda Forever”) original script.

Snoop Dogg is producing “Snoop,” which will incorporate music from his vast catalog, alongside Imagine Entertainment’s Brian Grazer (“8 Mile”) and Allan Mandelbaum and Death Row Pictures president Sara Ramaker. “Snoop” is the first project under Death Row Pictures’ overall deal with NBCUniversal Entertainment & Studios. Senior VP of production development Ryan Jones and director of development Tony Ducret will oversee the project for the studio.

articles.title: Ramayana: Rise of a Legend review – India’s most expensive film ever becomes spectacular, huge-scale epic
articles.summary: Based on the ancient classical poem about Rama, the avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu, this three-hour blockbuster is highly enjoyable. Here is a thoroughly engaging, rousing and spectacular Indian epic melodrama from director Nitesh Tiwari, with music by Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman, based on the…
body: Ranbir Kapoor plays the mythical Rama, a noble warrior and statesman who has been brought into being in the city state of Ayodhya as a bodily representative of Vishnu, and from the first his sense of destiny is overwhelming. But what exactly is that destiny? In broad terms, his fate is to face off with Ravana (Naveen “Yash” Kumar), king of far-off Lanka, a figure whose former slave status once triggered in him such a cosmically intense prayer for justice that Lord Brahma offered him the superpower of athletic strength and indifference to pain.

In Ayodhya, Rama marries the sweetly devoted Sita (Sai Pallavi), he enjoys an intense bond of comradeship with his brother Lakshmana (Ravi Dubey), and is the apple of his father’s eye; this is King Dasharatha (Arun Govil) who, careworn by affairs of state, is about cede the throne to Rama. But Rama’s stepmother Kaikeyi (Lara Dutta) furiously reminds Dasharatha that he promised the crown to Bharata (Adinath Kothare), the son they had together. Rama, Sita and Lakshmana are banished to the forest.

body: American singer-songwriter Sheryl Crow has described her "incredible" links to Wales, revealing that her mother's side of the family was from the country.

Crow, best known for hits including All I Wanna Do and If It Makes You Happy, said she did not know where exactly in Wales her family came from, but expressed a desire to research her heritage further.

articles.title: Tributes paid to drummer with dozens of number ones
articles.summary: Amarillo singer Tony Christie says Clem Cattini was a "world class" musician and gentleman.
body: Tributes have been paid after the death of drummer Clem Cattini, who performed on several UK Number One singles.

The 89-year-old, who lived in Hertfordshire, co-founded the Tornados in 1961. Their instrumental Telstar spent five weeks at the top of the UK chart in 1962, and they became the first British group to top the US Billboard Hot 100.

As a session musician, he played on number one hits such as Tom Jones' Green, Green Grass of Home, Dusty Springfield's You Don't Have To Say You Love Me and Tony Christie's (Is This the Way to) Amarillo?.
In a Facebook post, external Christie described Cattini as "a world class musician but also a world class gentleman".

articles.title: Judi Dench says Daniel Craig ordered her death. James Bond just got a lot scarier
articles.summary: Not only did Craig insist his 007 die at the end of his run, but now we learn from Dench’s memoir that it was his idea to kill her off too. How will the next Bond top that? Shoot a puppy?
body: Now that the next James Bond actor is on the brink of being unveiled, it may be a good time to take a proper look at the prior 007 with clear eyes. Because, while the reputations of all the previous Bonds have ossified over the years – in chronological order: sexy, wooden, camp, boring and silly – the Daniel Craig era is finally coming into focus. And it turns out that he was actually the angel of death.

Obviously anyone who saw No Time to Die knows this, because that film ended with Bond being exploded in a hail of missile fire. But according to Judi Dench’s new memoir Is It Too Late to Make a Run for It?, it was also Craig’s decision to kill off M, too.

In it, Dench tells of the moment she learned that her character would be sent to the glue factory in Skyfall. “I was taken to the Wolseley restaurant by Barbara [Broccoli], Michael [G Wilson] and Sam [Mendes] – I don’t think Daniel Craig was there – and they outlined the plot and told me they were going to bump me off,” she writes.
points: Not only did Craig insist his 007 die at the end of his run, but now we learn from Dench’s memoir that it was his idea to kill her off too.

articles.title: Female Filmmakers in Focus: Kelly O’Sullivan and Alex Thompson on “Mouse”
articles.summary: An interview with the Chicago-based filmmaking team on making intimate, character-driven films, moving forward with grief, and leveling up their directing partnership.
body: A few years back, Chicago-based directing duo Kelly O’Sullivan and Alex Thompson broke out big with “ Ghostlight,” their tender exploration of family (played by Chicago powerhouse acting family Keith Kupferer, Katherine Mallen Kupferer, and Tara Mallen) as they process an unimaginable loss through the power of community theatre. This year the duo have re-teamed with two-thirds of the Mallen Kupferer family for another exceptionally perceptive and honest depiction of grief and the rocky road towards healing.

Katherine Mallen Kupferer is Minnie, a high school junior who’s perfectly content playing second fiddle to her best friend Callie ( Chloe Coleman ), a theatre kid with her sights set on Juilliard and then Broadway glory. When an accident on the first day of summer break disrupts their close-knit friendship, Minnie must navigate senior year alone.
points: An interview with the Chicago-based filmmaking team on making intimate, character-driven films, moving forward with grief, and leveling up their directing partnership.
